config_fields.metric: Attention maps are resized to64x64, averaged then divided by their nonnegative total mass; target/control mass sums use the independently detected original-image color region. Lift subtracts mask pixel fraction, denominator4096. Color-area fractions are means over512x512 RGB masks, denominator262144 per generated image. Target_drop=original_fraction-target_edit_fraction; control_drop=original_fraction-control_edit_fraction. Quality HF is mean absolute adjacent-pixel difference for each axis, summed then divided by2*255. CLIP accuracy averages two diagonal-pair hits; positive margin averages both directional diagonal-minus-best-off-diagonal margins over the fixed two cases.
config_fields.predicate: For EACH of the two cases: target_control_gap>=.005 AND target_mass-mask_fraction>=.01 AND captured_map_count>=32; target_drop>=.05 AND target_drop>=control_drop+.05; target_color_fraction>=.02 AND normalized rgb_std>=.05 (the reported rgb_std is rgb.std()/255) AND HF<=.12; noise_HF>.12 AND noise_HF>=real_HF+.12. Across both originals: both CLIP directional accuracies>=1 AND mean_positive_margin>=2; peak allocated VRAM<=24GiB. preflight_passed is the conjunction; all listed comparisons are inclusive except noise_HF>.12. Use preserved unrounded values/booleans, not rounded figure labels.

The control is a fixed unrelated-token edit, not a random draw despite historical random_control field names. Noise uses independent CPU seed1000+case_seed. Binary question: does target attention mass in that shifted mask remain>=.20 AND control attention mass in the identical shifted mask remain<.20? Each mass sums the already normalized nonnegative map over the shifted mask; its normalization denominator is that maps complete64x64 attention sum before normalization, not region pixel count. Threshold comparisons use unrounded values. Target-only selectivity is insufficient if the control also reaches.20.
